ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, if the graph of the linear function $y_{1}=x+a$ intersects with the graph of the linear function $y_{2}=kx+b$ at point P(1,3), what is the solution set of the inequality $x+a\le kx+b$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the graph, when $x\leq 1$, $x+a\leq kx+b$,\\
that is, the solution set of the inequality $x+a\leq kx+b$ with respect to $x$ is $\boxed{x\leq 1}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are coordinate axes in the figure, and two straight lines intersect at the labeled point P. There are auxiliary dashed lines beside point P, showing that its x-coordinate is 1 and y-coordinate is 3, that is, P(1,3). The straight line y1=x+a slopes from the lower left to the upper right and is an increasing line; the straight line y2=kx+b slopes from the upper left to the lower right and is a decreasing line. Reasoning: The inequality x+a≤kx+b is equivalent to y1≤y2, that is, comparing the heights of the two straight lines at the same x. From the figure, it can be seen that to the left of the intersection point P, that is, when x<1, the increasing line y1 is below the decreasing line y2, so y1<y2; when x=1, the two lines intersect, so y1=y2; to the right of P, that is, when x>1, y1 is above y2, so y1>y2. Therefore the range of x satisfying y1≤y2 is x≤1.
